newsitem.title: CANADA: Methanex to take US$100 mln Q4 charge.
newsitem.headline: Methanex to take US$100 mln Q4 charge.

text.p: Methanex Corp said on Monday it would take a fourth-quarter charge of about US$100 million to write down the carrying value of several high-cost facilities that would be idled as part of the company's low-cost strategy.
Methanex said high-cost production at its Medicine Hat, Alberta and Waitara, New Zealand plants would be reduced or shut in as new Methanex low-cost capacity came on stream in Chile and New Zealand.

Methanex chief executive Pierre Choquette said the company's second plant in Chile, with a capacity of 925,000 tonnes, would come on stream in December 1996, while the recently approved third plant in Chile, with a capacity of 975,000 tonnes, was scheduled for start-up in the second half of 1999.

"Since we intend to match our production to our customer requirements, we will now reduce capacity at higher cost facilities as previously stated. In the short term this will impact production at Medicine Hat, Alberta," Choquette said.

He said that beginning in 1998, Methanex intended to concentrate the New Zealand production in the larger Motunui site to reduce costs further, while matching methanol production capability to contracted natural gas. The Waitara facility would therefore be idled.
Methanex said it would retain the flexibility to restart the plants.
